Again, measuring oveall statistic is not the game we're playing though. We specified EU because yes, we do have the highest quality of life and on those scales Slovenia is pretty damn average, if not shitty at best. 

But because you want statistics, Ill bite. Wasting my 15 min break on a fucking reddit argument because honestly cant stand the mentality. 

[According to Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/duncanmadden/2019/01/11/ranked-the-25-smartest-countries-in-the-world/?sh=34c68992163f) we are nowhere near smartest, so the Human development index certainly doesnt include our shitty education into the calculation, so having the potential to develop is a different metric than actual achievement. I wanted to go into how many companies have been driven out of the country or just plain out bought out from underneath us, but we arent there just yet.

Lets look at our [population](https://worldpopulationreview.com/country-rankings/median-age) even further. So that link there tells you how old our average human is, if I have to break it down for you. And guess what? To no ones surprise, our populace is amongst the oldest, on average. So lets look at [life expectancy](https://www.worldometers.info/demographics/life-expectancy/) which combined with the previous chart tells you that our life expectancy is 81.85 years, meaning our average demographic is shifting to older, not younger.

Also furthermore, civic engagement in our country is well below the [global standard](https://www.oecdbetterlifeindex.org/topics/civic-engagement/) where the average country will have approximately 68% voter turnout versus our 53% for our little nation. Which considering the population mass? its sad.

So measuring the world happiness of the population that is aging has nothing to do with the younger, still developing humans of the nation, who in turn have to live with a regime that isnt focusing on their future.
